pr_body:
This implements the integrity-only ciphers for TLS v1.3 defined in [RFC 9150](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9150#section-4) as requested in #18343.

Tests for the new cipher suites are implicitly added by `evp_libctx_test.c`.

Fixes #18343 

##### Checklist

- [x] documentation is added or updated
- [x] tests are added or updated

> @DDvO- Thank you for the review. I did the required changes.

Fine. Just a few follow-up points - see above the the comments that I did not mark as resolved.

A general question, maybe to the OpenSSL team:

Do the tests that are referenced here include the test case that a TLS record is rejected in case its integrity gets violated in transit?

I would like to know the procedure for requesting an OTC review. Is there any action required from my side?

> I would like to know the procedure for requesting an OTC review. Is there any action required from my side?

No, there is no further action needed for now.

This PR throws up a number of questions for OTC to consider:

**OTC: This is based on an informational track RFC. Are we ok with integrating support on that basis?**

**OTC: This changes the public `EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH` from 16 to 48 - which is not allowed in a minor release. How should we handle this situation? Similarly `EVP_MAX_AEAD_TAG_LENGTH` changes from 16 to 48**

**OTC: This is implemented by adding a new AEAD based EVP_CIPHER - but there is no standard for such a standalone cipher - it is only specified for use within a TLS context (and via an informational track RFC as noted above). In reality this is just a MAC packaged as an EVP_CIPHER. Are we ok with that?**

Adding an OTC hold until the above are considered.

@mattcaswell Do you have any idea what would be the rough complexity in comparison to this PR of implementing this directly inside libssl maybe with the help of the existing NULL cipher? libssl can handle separate cipher + mac calls for TLS-1.2 so I assume it would be fairly simply possible to add the same for these TLS-1.3 integrity-only ciphers.

> @mattcaswell Do you have any idea what would be the rough complexity in comparison to this PR of implementing this directly inside libssl maybe with the help of the existing NULL cipher? libssl can handle separate cipher + mac calls for TLS-1.2 so I assume it would be fairly simply possible to add the same for these TLS-1.3 integrity-only ciphers.

The TLSv1.3 code was implemented on the assumption that all future ciphersuites would be AEAD based. We did not implement the code path for separate cipher + mac like it exists in TLSv1.2 and below. There are all sorts of complexities in the TLSv1.2 code with that - mainly due to potential side channels that can occur in the (now outdated) mac-then-encrypt case.

It would definitely be possible to implement something similar in the TLSv1.3 case - but I would probably leave it as two possibilities: AEAD or MAC only (i.e. not try and implement cipher + mac). The main substance of the change would require a new codepath in this function I imagine:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/0f644b96d209443b4566f7e86e3be2568292e75b/ssl/record/methods/tls13_meth.c#L58-L176

We also need updates to set up an EVP_MAC ctx somewhere. Probably here:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/0f644b96d209443b4566f7e86e3be2568292e75b/ssl/record/methods/tls13_meth.c#L16-L56

In terms of relative complexity between this PR and that approach, I would not expect the alternative approach to be any more complex (although its definitely not trivial). Mostly because it can just use the existing libcrypto HMAC primitives without needing to invent a new AEAD cipher. Doing it this way would avoid OTC issues 2 and 3 that I raised above.

> **OTC: This is based on an informational track RFC. Are we ok with integrating support on that basis?**

A note on this OTC issue:

AFAIK, [RFC 9150](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9150) is informational because the standardisation of TLS at IETF is strongly driven by web PKI security and tries to avoid pitfalls for native users who, when using integrity-only ciphers with HTTPS servers, might assume that they have a "secure" connection while in this case they would not get confidentiality.
This is why - for the general use - the authors of TLS v1.3 kicked out integrity-only cipher suites.

Yet as motivated for instance in [RFC 9150 section 4](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9150#section-4), there are various good use cases for cipher suites in TLS that only provide authentication and integrity protection, in particular in industrial automation, safety-critical infrastructures, and IoT. In particular, this feature is important for some of our product lines.

I'm surprised that now, after a full PR with code and tests is available, this has been raised as a concern, whereas @mattcaswell [had written in May 2022](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/18343#issuecomment-1131485621) on the respective feature request:
> Sounds interesting. I'm not aware of anyone working on this.

> I'm surprised that now, after a full PR with code and tests is available, this has been raised as a concern, whereas @mattcaswell https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/18343#issuecomment-1131485621 on the respective feature request:

To be clear - I am not against integrating support for integrity only ciphersuites based on this RFC. I can see that they could be useful in some scenarios. It was merely a point that I noted during my detailed review of the PR that I thought OTC should be aware of.
I would prefer if this was implemented via direct EVP_MAC calls in libssl. This kind of overloading the cipher concept with AEAD with no encryption seems wrong to me.

**OTC: We are OK with including support for integrity-only ciphers according to RFC 9150.**

**OTC: The EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH and EVP_MAX_AEAD_TAG_LENGTH macros cannot be changed in 3.x versions as that breaks API and ABI stability requirements.**

For the third question we have an OTC action to establish a policy on integrity only ciphersuites.
Issue for that action: https://github.com/openssl/project/issues/434

Thank you for these answers.

> **OTC: We are OK with including support for integrity-only ciphers according to RFC 9150.**

Glad to hear.
 
> **OTC: The `EVP_MAX_IV_LENGTH` and `EVP_MAX_AEAD_TAG_LENGTH` macros cannot be changed in 3.x versions as that breaks API and ABI stability requirements.**

I understand - while it would be very unfortunate if inclusion of the feature had to wait until OpenSSL 4.0 😦
I wonder why these two constants are exported in the public API after all?
It feels like they are actually implementation details that should not have been published.
In general, TLS needs to be flexible on the IV and AEAD tag lengths,
and these two constant macros pose an artificial upper bounds to them.

Do you see any way of still accommodating 48 bytes long IVs and AEAD tag lengths,
or maybe a way of ignoring these macros when the new integrity-only ciphers are being used?

> For the third question we have an OTC action to establish a policy on integrity only ciphersuites. Issue for that action: [openssl/project#434](https://github.com/openssl/project/issues/434)

Nice. So looks like here @rajeev-0 should wait for the outcome before he can sensibly do any adaptations, right?

> I understand - while it would be very unfortunate if inclusion of the feature had to wait until OpenSSL 4.0 😦
I wonder why these two constants are exported in the public API after all?
It feels like they are actually implementation details that should not have been published.
In general, TLS needs to be flexible on the IV and AEAD tag lengths,
and these two constant macros pose an artificial upper bounds to them.

Yes, this is definitely a problem with our API. With providers we can no longer know what the "MAX" size of something is, because a provider could come along an plug in an algorithm with something bigger. OTOH these macros are definitely used, and can be quite useful for stack allocation purposes (e.g. stack allocate an array big enough to hold the largest IV that I'm going to ever need). Our OTC discussion prompted us to raise this issue:

https://github.com/openssl/project/issues/435

> Do you see any way of still accommodating 48 bytes long IVs and AEAD tag lengths,
or maybe a way of ignoring these macros when the new integrity-only ciphers are being used?

Option 2 in openssl/project#434 would avoid the issue entirely since it doesn't need to plug in a new cipher. If we go with option 1 then that would imply implementing a cipher that does not conform to these MAX values (which seems like a bad idea to me).

> Nice. So looks like here @rajeev-0 should wait for the outcome before he can sensibly do any adaptations, right?

Yes, waiting until we reach some consensus on this seems like a good idea.

issue_context.title: TLS 1.3: add 'integrity-only' cipher suites
issue_context.body:
In comparison to earlier versions, regular TLS 1.3 does no more offer cipher suites without encryption.
On the other hand, as motivated for instance in [RFC 9150 section 4](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9150#section-4), there are various use cases for cipher suites in TLS that only provide authentication and integrity protection, in particular in industrial automation and IoT.
So far, such use cases cannot be implemented with TLS 1.3 and thus are stuck with TLS 1.2, at least when based on OpenSSL.

This feature request is for optionally supporting the cipher suites `TLS_SHA256_SHA256` and `TLS_SHA384_SHA384` as defined in  [RFC 9150 section 4 to 8](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9150#section-4).

There is already a PoC implementation of 2019/20 by Yiannis Stavrou of Nozomi Networks: https://github.com/NozomiNetworks/openssl/commits/enull-tls13-openssl111 based on OpenSSL 1.1.1.
I just had a look at it and rebased it locally to the current master.
I did not spend effort on figuring out whether it is correct and fully functional, 
but just found that the general TLS tests have not been adapted/extended to it, and so far a number of them fail.
Is there anyone who has already taken this development further or has done an independent implementation based on OpenSSL?
comments: Sounds interesting. I'm not aware of anyone working on this.

review_comments: Since you potentially duped `mac_ctx`, this and all subsequent `return 0` need to be replaced by `goto err`
refactored the code and introduced `end_mac` to always free the `mac_ctx` within the same code block.
In case `ctx == NULL` you now return an error but do not call `memmove` nor return 1. Is this on purpose?
Here `ctx == NULL` check was irrelevant, because if `ctx` is NULL then `EVP_CIPHER_CTX_get0_cipher` will return NULL.
I'd suggest that we move the creation of mdctx until just before the call to `ssl_md` below

or maybe just a leftover of the earlier version?
If it is needed for the new integrity-only feature, maybe add a respective comment.
It is a bugfix, as It lead to crash when NULL cipher is used with TLS v1.3.
I'd prefer `inl != 0 && !ossl_assert(out != NULL) && in != out` - please verify that it was called with inl == 0 when it was crashing.  If not, that is a bug at the caller.
It crashes if this is used as AEAD cipher and `EVP_CipherUpdate` is called for AAD (additional authenticated data) where `out == NULL` and `inl != 0`.
Ah! Good point, I've forgot about that awkward API use case. But then should that AAD call be skipped at the caller if we are using the integrity only ciphersuites? Or would it be too complex change?

We are not using it in integrity only ciphers for TLS 1.3. I could just remove this modification without any issue.

But if it doesn't create any issue, then it will be nice that null cipher can also be used as other ciphers without any specific consideration.
OK then
Thanks for updating the variable name to `nonce_len` as I suggested to avoid confusion.
Not sure I understand why the scope of this was changed?
It was done to remove the multiple call to `EVP_MD_CTX_free(mdctx)`. But your suggestion regarding relocation of creation of `mdctx` looks better.
Don't we leak the `mac_ctx` here?
As `mac_ctx = rl->mac_ctx`, and it get free by function `static void tls_int_free(OSSL_RECORD_LAYER *rl)` . I tried to replicate the implementation of `rl->enc_ctx`.
Ah right - of course.

Are you sure to free here the right value of `mac_md`, 
also in case `!(which & SSL3_CC_EARLY)`, which can also lead to an assignment to `mac_md` above?

As we have just discussed, it's correct because the `ssl_evp_md_free(mac_md);` is done only if
`(which & SSL3_CC_EARLY) != 0 `while the mentioned assignment to `mac_md` further above
is only in case `(which & SSL3_CC_EARLY) == 0`, so in a different (non-early) situation.

Turns out that I was confused by the expression `!(which & SSL3_CC_EARLY)`, in the original line 601,
which is not according to the coding style.
So please update that original guard`!(which & SSL3_CC_EARLY)` to `(which & SSL3_CC_EARLY) == 0`,
as well as, more further up, update `(which & SSL3_CC_EARLY)` to `(which & SSL3_CC_EARLY) != 0`.

Since meanwhile `cipher = EVP_CIPHER_CTX_get0_cipher(ctx);` moved to further down, which is good,
the condition `ctx == NULL` is no more redundant (your [argument of April 3](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/22903/files#r1549890920) no more holds),
so now must revert to the original `ctx == NULL || rec->type == SSL3_RT_ALERT`
as otherwise `ivlen = EVP_CIPHER_CTX_get_iv_length(ctx);` will crash on `ctx == NULL`
As just discussed , I added a comment `/* enc_ctx is ignored when rl->mac_ctx != NULL */`. 
Therefore no crash can occur in the below code if it is NULL.

So I was wrong, thanks for explaining.
With the new comment on `ctx` (which is now called `enc_ctx`) it should be clear.
